les: Die naaldwoud: bome wat die lang winter uithou
kaps_punt: Ligging op Aarde | Klimaat: temperatuur - en reënvalpatrone (maandelikse gemiddeldes) | Natuurlike plantegroei en wildlewe in 'n naaldwoud

items.bewering: Die grootste naaldwoude lê in 'n breë band oor die verre noorde van die wêreld.
items.blok: Waar die naaldwoude lê
items.bron: Big Think 'A pyramid map of the world's biomes' (https://bigthink.com/strange-maps/a-pyramid-map-of-the-worlds-biomes/): the boreal forest/taiga is the world's largest land biome; Sage Encyclopedia of Geography 'Biome: boreal forest' (https://sk.sagepub.com/ency/edvol/embed/geography/chpt/biome-boreal-forest); Wikipedia 'Taiga' (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taiga): a circumpolar belt at roughly 50°N-70°N. The superlative holds: the largest coniferous forests are the boreal belt. Other coniferous forests exist (e.g. temperate coniferous forest of the Pacific Northwest), and the next sentence correctly narrows the lesson to this band.

items.bewering: Die band loop deur Kanada, die noorde van Europa en die noorde van Rusland.
items.blok: Waar die naaldwoude lê
items.bron: Wikipedia 'Taiga' (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taiga) lists Russia, Canada, the US and Scandinavia; Big Think (as above): main expanses across Scandinavia, Russia, Alaska and Canada. Tested as a set: all three named regions are correct. The list is incomplete rather than false: Alaska (and smaller parts of Mongolia, Kazakhstan, China and Japan) also carry the band, and in Siberia the taiga reaches well south of the 'north' of Russia. No false contrast is created, so no correction is required.

items.bewering: In die verre suide van die wêreld is daar nie so 'n band nie.
items.blok: Waar die naaldwoude lê
items.bron: Sage Encyclopedia of Geography 'Biome: boreal forest' (https://sk.sagepub.com/ency/edvol/embed/geography/chpt/biome-boreal-forest): no equivalent belt exists in the Southern Hemisphere; Big Think (as above) says the same.

items.bewering: Op dieselfde afstand suid van die ewenaar lê daar byna net see. 'n Woud kan net op land groei.
items.blok: Waar die naaldwoude lê
items.bron: Sage Encyclopedia of Geography (as above): no southern belt 'since large land masses at similar latitudes are not found there'; av8n.com 'Land and water by latitude' (https://av8n.com/physics/land-water-latitude.htm): very little land between 45°S and 65°S and a band near 60°S with no land at all; Wikipedia 'Circles of latitude between the 50th and 55th parallel south' (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Circles_of_latitude_between_the_50th_parallel_south_and_the_55th_parallel_south): only the tip of South America and small islands. Quantifier 'byna net' holds: the only land at 50-65°S is southern Patagonia, small islands and the tip of the Antarctic Peninsula; the coast of Antarctica enters only at the far edge (about 66-70°S), and it is ice-covered. Writer note only, no change required.

items.bewering: Die naaldwoud het 'n lang winter wat baie koud is. Die somer is kort en sag.
items.blok: 'n Lang winter en 'n kort somer
items.bron: Wikipedia 'Taiga' (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taiga): 'the long, cold winter is the dominant feature'; below-freezing winters last 5-7 months, summers only 1-3 months, an average summer day 18 °C; Siberian coldest-month means -6 °C to -50 °C. NASA Science 'Coniferous forest' biome page (https://science.nasa.gov/kids/earth/mission-biomes/bioconiferous): 'cold, long, snowy winters'. 'Sag' (mild) fits summer means of roughly 10-20 °C, though interior Siberia and Alaska have hot days.

items.bewering: Die maandelikse gemiddeldes wys 'n groot verskil tussen die koudste en die warmste maand.
items.blok: 'n Lang winter en 'n kort somer
items.bron: Britannica, Köppen subarctic climate (via search; https://www.britannica.com:443/print/article/134997): annual ranges larger than in any other climate type on Earth, over 60 °C in central Siberia; Ohio University 'Subarctic climate' (https://people.ohio.edu/dyer/TPE/tpe_3e/climate_systems/subarctic.html): 'the largest annual temperature range of any climate'; Yakutsk annual range about 63 °C. 'Koudste' and 'warmste' here only name the two months being compared and are used correctly.

items.bewering: Dit is 'n groter verskil as in die reënwoud of in die warm woestyn.
items.blok: 'n Lang winter en 'n kort somer
items.bron: Britannica and Ohio University (as above): the subarctic has the largest annual range of any climate. Rainforest: Manaus monthly means about 27-31 °C, a range of about 3-4 °C (Meteostat-based table via kupi.com, https://kupi.com/en/explore/brazil/manaus/weather; Internet Geography, https://www.internetgeography.net/topics/what-is-the-climate-of-the-rainforest/). Hot desert: Wikipedia 'Desert climate' (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Desert_climate) station charts (Sabha, Baghdad, Las Vegas) give coldest-to-warmest monthly mean ranges of about 19-25 °C. The comparison concerns monthly averages, so the desert's large day-night swing does not undercut it, and the mapping holds. Coastal edges of the boreal zone have smaller ranges, but the general claim about the type stands.

items.bewering: Daar val nie baie reën in 'n jaar nie en in die winter val die water meestal as sneeu.
items.blok: 'n Lang winter en 'n kort somer
items.bron: NASA Science coniferous-forest page (as above): 300-900 mm a year; Wikipedia 'Taiga': generally 200-750 mm, 1 000 mm in some areas, falling mainly as summer rain but also as snow; EBSCO Research Starters 'Boreal forests and taiga' (https://ebsco.com/research-starters/earth-and-atmospheric-sciences/boreal-forests-and-taiga): 300-850 mm. Winter precipitation in a climate with sub-zero winter months falls as snow. The sentence correctly says only that WINTER precipitation is mostly snow, not that most of the year's precipitation is snow.

items.bewering: Die sneeu smelt nie dadelik nie en hoop maande lank op. Daarom lê die sneeu diep al val daar min water.
items.blok: 'n Lang winter en 'n kort somer
items.bron: Sturm snow-climate classification, as summarised in Cambridge 'Differences in compaction behavior of three climate classes of snow' (https://resolve.cambridge.org/core/services/aop-cambridge-core/content/view/8DDC5847E25986054DC3878DF2F5B213/S0260305500014683a.pdf/differences-in-compaction-behavior-of-three-climate-classes-of-snow.pdf) and Slaughter & Benson 1982 (https://arc.lib.montana.edu/snow-science/objects/issw-1982-011-012.pdf): taiga snow is 0.6-1.5 m deep and of very low density (about 0.20 g/cm3), attributed to long snow residence times. NASA 'Snow sleuths' (https://science.nasa.gov/earth/earth-observatory/snow-sleuths): snow lies in the boreal forest for up to six months; Wikipedia 'Taiga': up to nine months in the far north. The causal chain (snow lies for months, so a deep layer builds up from modest precipitation) is sound. Eastern Siberia is shallower, but 'diep' holds for the type.

items.bewering: Op die Januariekaart lê hierdie band diep in die koue streke. In die noorde van die wêreld val Januarie in die winter en Julie in die somer.
items.blok: Wat die kaarte van hierdie band wys
items.bron: Wikipedia 'Taiga': Siberian coldest-month (January) means -6 °C to -50 °C; NASA Science coniferous page: winter averages down to -40 °C. In the Northern Hemisphere January falls in winter and July in summer. On a January mean-temperature map the 50-70°N continental band carries some of the lowest values outside Antarctica (Ohio University subarctic page, as above).

items.bewering: Op die Juliekaart is dieselfde band veel minder koud.
items.blok: Wat die kaarte van hierdie band wys
items.bron: Wikipedia 'Taiga': average summer day about 18 °C; the band is often bounded by the 10 °C July isotherm to the north. NASA Science coniferous page: summer averages around 10 °C. Compared with January means of -20 to -40 °C this is 'veel minder koud'.

items.bewering: Die reënvalkaart wys oor die grootste deel van die band minder reën as in die reënwoud.
items.blok: Wat die kaarte van hierdie band wys
items.bron: NASA Science coniferous page: 300-900 mm; FAO, K. Kuusela on boreal forests (https://www.fao.org/3/u6850e/u6850e03.htm): 400-800 mm, eastern Siberia 300-400 mm; tropical rainforest normally above 1 750-2 000 mm (Wärtsilä encyclopedia, https://wartsila.com/encyclopedia/term/tropical-rainforest-climate; Wikipedia 'Rainforest'). 'Oor die grootste deel' is if anything cautious: even the wettest boreal areas (about 1 000 mm) fall below rainforest totals.

items.bewering: Twee kaarte is dus nodig om hierdie plek se hele jaar te wys.
items.blok: Wat die kaarte van hierdie band wys
items.bron: Follows from the sources above: in the boreal zone January is about the coldest month and July about the warmest (Yakutsk, Fairbanks pattern; Wikipedia 'Taiga'), so the two monthly mean-temperature maps bracket the annual range, and given the 30-60 °C difference neither map alone represents the year. This is a reading claim rather than a fact claim, and it is sound for temperature. Writer note: it follows a sentence about the rainfall map, so 'twee kaarte' refers back to the two temperature maps.

items.bewering: Die natuurlike plantegroei van 'n naaldwoud is meestal bome met blare soos smal naalde.
items.blok: Die natuurlike plantegroei: naalde en keëls
items.bron: Hinterland Who's Who / Environment and Climate Change Canada boreal forest factsheet (https://www.hww.ca/assets/pdfs/factsheets/boreal-forest-factsheet.pdf): dominated by conifers (spruce, fir, pine, tamarack), with broad-leaf aspen, poplar and birch also widespread. The quantifier 'meestal' is correct, since broadleaf trees are present but do not dominate.

items.bewering: 'n Naald verloor minder water as 'n breë blaar.
items.blok: Die natuurlike plantegroei: naalde en keëls
items.bron: Wikipedia 'Taiga': 'The adaptation of evergreen needles limits the water lost due to transpiration'; Open University 'Surviving the winter' (https://www.open.edu/openlearn/nature-environment/natural-history/surviving-the-winter/content-section-1.3.1): needles have a small surface area for their volume, a waxy cuticle and sunken stomata, which reduce water loss; HWW factsheet: thick waxy coatings protect against drying winds.

items.bewering: In plaas van blomme dra hierdie naaldbome keëls met saad daarin.
items.blok: Die natuurlike plantegroei: naalde en keëls
items.bron: NASA Science coniferous page: 'grow needles instead of leaves and cones instead of flowers'; Arnold Arboretum, Harvard (https://arboretum.harvard.edu/collections/conifer-collection): conifer seeds are protected in cones rather than in fruits. Every boreal genus (spruce, pine, fir, larch) bears woody seed cones, so 'hierdie naaldbome' holds for the trees of this forest.

items.bewering: Die meeste naaldbome hou hulle naalde die hele jaar.
items.blok: Die natuurlike plantegroei: naalde en keëls
items.bron: Penn State Extension 'The distinctive features of conifers' (https://ecosystems.psu.edu/research/centers/private-forests/news/the-distinctive-features-of-conifers): of 71 conifer genera, 65 are evergreen; NASA Science coniferous page: conifers bear needles all year long. The quantifier 'die meeste' is correct. Evergreens shed individual needles gradually but are never bare.

items.bewering: In hierdie naaldwoud laat een soort naaldboom sy naalde in die herfs val.
items.blok: Die natuurlike plantegroei: naalde en keëls
items.bron: HWW boreal factsheet: tamarack (a larch) 'loses its needles each fall', the exception among Canada's boreal conifers; Wikipedia 'Taiga': 'larch ... is deciduous'; Bartlett Arboretum / Penn State: larches are among the few deciduous conifers, and the others (bald cypress, dawn redwood, golden larch, Chinese swamp cypress) are not boreal. 'Een soort' is correct where 'soort' means a kind of tree, the larch. Writer note: the larch is a genus with several species in this band (tamarack in Canada; Siberian, Dahurian/Gmelin and Cajander larch in Russia), so the sentence would be false only if 'soort' were read as one botanical species.

items.bewering: Woude van hierdie boom dek 'n enorme deel van die noorde van Rusland.
items.blok: Die natuurlike plantegroei: naalde en keëls
items.bron: GEF/Taiga Rescue Network report (https://www.gef.or.jp/activityex/forest/fairwood/book/taiga1999/report/taiga_e1.PDF): larch-dominated forest is 36.6% of Russia's forest area; NASA technical report (https://ntrs.nasa.gov/citations/20110022650): about 40%; larch dominates the vast territory of eastern Siberia (Hokkaido University review, https://eprints.lib.hokudai.ac.jp/repo/huscap/all/24482/10(1)_P19-29.pdf).

items.bewering: Die bome staan dikwels dig bymekaar.
items.blok: Die natuurlike plantegroei: naalde en keëls
items.bron: Wikipedia 'Taiga': the southern closed-canopy forest has 'many closely-spaced trees and mossy groundcover'; dark taiga of spruce and fir forms a dense canopy (floraveg.eu and Czech Journal of Forest Science results for 'light taiga'/'dark taiga', https://floraveg.eu/habitat/overview/T3H). 'Dikwels' is the right quantifier.

items.bewering: Die woudvloer is dikwels met mos, korsmos en lae struike bedek.
items.blok: Die natuurlike plantegroei: naalde en keëls
items.bron: HWW boreal factsheet: mosses form a complete carpet under conifers, open areas are carpeted with lichens, and low shrubs (blueberry, willow, alder) occur; Wikipedia 'Taiga': mossy groundcover, and lichens and mosses on the forest floor; Huntington taiga notes (https://huntington.org/sites/default/files/volunteer-academy/b3c2taiga.pdf): open larch forests have understories of shrubs, mosses and lichens. Tested as a set: all three belong on the boreal forest floor, and none is out of place.

items.bewering: Party naaldwoude is oop en lig met baie ruimte tussen die bome.
items.blok: Die natuurlike plantegroei: naalde en keëls
items.bron: Wikipedia 'Taiga': 'lichen woodland or sparse taiga, with trees that are farther-spaced'; 'light taiga' is the established term for open larch forest (floraveg.eu T3H, https://floraveg.eu/habitat/overview/T3H; Huntington notes: larch forests 'are open').

items.bewering: Die wildlewe van die naaldwoud in Kanada moet elke jaar 'n lang winter deurkom.
items.blok: Die wildlewe kom die winter deur
items.bron: Wikipedia 'Taiga': below-freezing winters last 5-7 months; NASA 'Snow sleuths': snow lies in Canada's boreal forest for up to six months.

items.bewering: Die wolf se pels word in die winter dik en hy jag deur die koue.
items.blok: Die wildlewe kom die winter deur
items.bron: Northwest Trek 'Warm winter coats' (https://www.nwtrek.org/warm-winter-coats/): the wolf's dense undercoat grows thick in autumn and is shed in spring; People and Carnivores 'Wolves in the winter' (https://peopleandcarnivores.org/blog/wolves-in-the-winter): wolves do not hibernate or migrate and stay active all winter; Alaska Dept of Fish and Game (https://www.adfg.alaska.gov/index.cfm%3Fadfg=intensivemanagement.predatorprey): wolves are major predators in the boreal forest of northern Canada and interior Alaska.

items.bewering: Die swartbeer soek 'n hol en slaap deur 'n groot deel van die winter.
items.blok: Die wildlewe kom die winter deur
items.bron: Wildlife Biology (BioOne, https://complete.bioone.org/journals/Wildlife-Biology/volume-20/issue-4/wlb.00037/Application-of-a-species-distribution-model-to-identify-and-manage/10.2981/wlb.00037.full): at northern latitudes black bears may hibernate for up to seven months; Nova Scotia Wildlife Park (https://wildlifepark.novascotia.ca/species/american-black-bear) and Journey North (https://journeynorth.org/tm/spring/BearYear.html): black bears den through winter with near-continuous sleep for 4-6 months; Ursus 2014 range survey (https://bioone.org/journals/ursus/volume-25/issue-1/URSUS-D-12-00020.1/Geographic-distribution-of-American-black-bears-in-North-America/10.2192/URSUS-D-12-00020.1.full): black bears live across Canada, including the boreal forest. 'Slaap' is an acceptable simplification of bear hibernation, in which body temperature drops only slightly.

items.bewering: Baie voëls trek in die herfs weg en kom terug wanneer die lente kos bring.
items.blok: Die wildlewe kom die winter deur
items.bron: Pew Charitable Trusts '5 reasons the boreal forest is important to migratory birds' (https://www.pewtrusts.org/en/research-and-analysis/articles/2021/05/07/5-reasons-the-boreal-forest-is-important-to-migratory-birds): 1-3 billion birds fly north each spring to breed and up to 5 billion leave each fall; Boreal Songbird Initiative 'North America's bird nursery' (https://www.borealbirds.org/node/9531). 'Baie' rather than 'alle' is correct, since some birds stay all year. Tested as a set (wolf, black bear, birds): they show three real and distinct strategies (staying active with a thicker coat, hibernating in a den, migrating), and the set implies no false contrast.

items.bewering: Hierdie streek is koud waar die reënwoud en die warm woestyn warm is.
items.blok: Hoe hierdie streek van die ander twee verskil
items.bron: Wikipedia 'Taiga': mean annual temperature -5 to 5 °C; rainforest monthly means about 27-31 °C (Manaus, as above); hot-desert hot-month means 29-35 °C (Wikipedia 'Desert climate'). True as a characterisation of each region's year. The mapping holds as long as it is read as the annual picture: a boreal July (about 16-19 °C) can be warmer than a hot desert's January (about 10-13 °C), and the lesson's own 'somer is sag' sentence keeps a learner from over-reading it.

items.bewering: Dit het 'n egte winter en 'n egte somer, waar die reënwoud se maande eenders lyk.
items.blok: Hoe hierdie streek van die ander twee verskil
items.bron: Internet Geography rainforest climate page (as above) and the Manaus monthly table: rainforest monthly temperature means stay within about 3-4 °C, so there is no winter or summer; Wikipedia 'Taiga': a very large seasonal range. Writer note: the clause holds for temperature, which is what the winter-and-summer contrast is about. Many rainforests (including central Amazonia) have clearly wetter and drier months, so the sentence should not be widened to say the rainfall bars look the same.

items.bewering: Oor enorme gebiede groei min soorte boom en in die reënwoud groei baie soorte saam.
items.blok: Hoe hierdie streek van die ander twee verskil
items.bron: Wikipedia 'Taiga': 'Very few species, in four main genera, are found', 'low botanical diversity'; FAO (https://www.fao.org/4/ad111e/AD111E04.htm) and associated results: about 200-300 tree species in a single hectare of Amazon forest, against about 4 species per hectare around 50° latitude; the boreal forest is dominated by a handful of spruce, pine, fir and larch species.

items.bewering: naaldwoud: 'n Woud waar die meeste bome naalde in plaas van breë blare het.
items.blok: naaldwoud
items.bron: Read alone: an accurate definition of a forest dominated by needle-leaved trees. HWW boreal factsheet and Wikipedia 'Taiga' (forest of mostly needle-leaved conifers, with some broadleaf trees). The quantifier 'die meeste' correctly leaves room for the birch, aspen and poplar present.

items.bewering: naaldboom: 'n Boom met smal naalde as blare, wat gewoonlik keëls dra.
items.blok: naaldboom
items.bron: Read alone: accurate for the word 'naaldboom' (needle tree) and for every boreal conifer. Penn State and Harvard Arboretum (as above): conifers bear cones; Wikipedia 'Conifer cone' (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Conifer_cone): fleshy cones in juniper and yew, which 'gewoonlik' correctly covers. Writer note only: some conifers worldwide have scale or flat leaves (cypress; South Africa's own yellowwood, Podocarpus), so this entry describes a needle tree rather than every conifer. That is fine as long as the entry is not later reused as a definition of all conifers.

items.bewering: keël: Die deel met skubbe waarin die meeste naaldbome hulle saad dra.
items.blok: keël
items.bron: Read alone: Wikipedia 'Conifer cone' (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Conifer_cone): a seed-bearing organ with scales arranged round an axis; seeds develop on the seed scales of the female cone. 'Die meeste' is correct: yew, with its aril, and the podocarps are exceptions. Writer note: conifers also have small pollen cones that carry no seed, but the entry describes the seed cone correctly and does not say every cone holds seed.

items.bewering: korsmos: 'n Swam en 'n klein lewende ding wat kos uit sonlig maak, wat saam groei.
items.blok: korsmos
items.bron: Read alone: Wikipedia 'Symbiosis in lichens' (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Symbiosis_in_lichens) and British Lichen Society 'What is a lichen?' (https://britishlichensociety.org.uk/learning/what-is-a-lichen): a stable partnership between a fungus and a photosynthetic partner (a green alga in about 90%, or a cyanobacterium), in which the photobiont makes food by photosynthesis. Accurate simplification. It correctly does not call a lichen a moss, despite the Afrikaans name.

opsomming: All 33 checkable claims in this coniferous-forest lesson hold up against web sources, including the superlatives, every quantifier, the three sets (forest floor, wildlife, larch) and the comparisons with the rainforest and the hot desert. The only notes are precision points for the writer, none needing a change: 'een soort naaldboom' is right only as one kind of tree, the larch, and the clause saying the rainforest's months look alike holds for temperature but not for rainfall.
